page: Microsoft Azure M96bds_v3 is an x86_64 server belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a 410 GB local SSD alongside premium block storage capabilities.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 7,441.98 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 184.62 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by top-tier results in bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU scores. The server also excels in database operations, static web serving throughput, and cryptographic tasks. Single-core performance and single-threaded decompression fall within the average range, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to fully leverage the hardware.

Given its high resource density, the M96bds_v3 offers qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise-scale deployments requiring massive memory footprints and high-throughput parallel processing without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The combination of 768 GB of RAM, dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon cores, and local SSD storage makes this server highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory data analytics, heavy multi-threaded compilation, and medium-to-large LLM inference prompt processing.
description: The Microsoft Azure M96bds_v3 is a high-capacity, memory-optimized server from the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. Powered by a dedicated 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz, it features 768.0 GB of RAM and a 410 GB local SSD. The architecture supports advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512 and AMX), driving top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations. While single-core performance remains average, the server's massive parallel processing capabilities and high memory-to-core ratio deliver excellent qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive enterprise workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory analytics, and multi-threaded data processing.
